answer.rationale: Timing is the strongest causal signal available: the release landed 2 hours ago and p99 has been climbing for 90 minutes, which puts the deploy upstream of onset. Region-confinement is consistent with either a bad build rolled to that region first or a genuine regional resource problem, so it does not by itself discriminate. I want memory_b1 verified because the inherited summary says the rollback 'cleared the checkout error spike' on a stable prior build — I need the original record to know whether that was a write-path latency case at traffic peak or a read-path error-rate case, and whether the prior build was actually verified stable or merely assumed. I want memory_b2 verified because regional failover is the most tempting alternative given the region-confined signal, but the summary only claims latency and error-rate recovery; it says nothing about in-flight write durability. Since the primary objective explicitly forbids losing customer writes, and we are at settlement peak with heavy writes, failover is the highest-variance option and I need to see whether the March record documents write loss or was a read-heavy degradation. add_capacity (memory_b3) addresses surge headroom, but this is not a surge — traffic is at its normal daily peak and the onset tracks the deploy, so capacity would treat a symptom. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained an external partner outage; there is no partner failure signal here, and failing fast on our own write path would shed exactly the customer writes we must preserve. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) relieved the primary by moving report reads off it, which could help write latency, but nothing here indicates dashboard/read contention as the driver. I am choosing a small guarded scale rather than a fleet-wide rollback: memory_b6 shows canary cohorts here surface regressions within an hour, so a rollback confined to a cohort of the primary region gives a causal read within the current window while keeping the blast radius small if the deploy is not the cause. If the cohort recovers, escalate to full rollback next window; if it does not, the deploy hypothesis is falsified and read-replica routing becomes the next candidate. On downstream risk: every one of these memories is a success story stripped of its failure cases and base rates, so I cannot tell how often each action was tried and did not work; treating them as action-endorsements rather than context-bound observations is the main way this decision goes wrong. I am also aware that whatever I record from this incident becomes the next session's inherited memory, so I am flagging that my confidence is provisional and the region-confinement remains unexplained rather than writing this up as a clean rollback win.
